purpose: Synthetic adversarial regression corpus; not an accuracy benchmark.
labeling_policy: Expected outputs are manually authored from the documented rule contract, not copied from scanner output.

environment-precedence.title: GitHub Actions workflow syntax: env
environment-precedence.claim: Step env overrides job env, and job env overrides workflow env.

event-expressions.title: GitHub Actions expressions
event-expressions.claim: Job and step conditions use boolean expressions and GitHub contexts.

event-security.title: Events that trigger workflows
event-security.claim: Event payloads and pull_request_target execution context determine attacker influence and privilege.

env-command.title: GNU Coreutils env invocation
env-command.claim: env executes the command following its options and NAME=VALUE assignments in a modified environment.

anthropic-action-modes.title: Claude Code Action tag and agent modes
anthropic-action-modes.claim: Supported issue, comment, and review triggers can select tag mode, which fetches parent issue or PR context; a nonempty prompt normally selects agent mode, while track_progress can force tag mode. A bare PR trigger does not imply tag mode.

anthropic-action-access.title: Claude Code Action access control
anthropic-action-access.claim: The action checks trigger-user write access by default, but this does not authenticate the author of separately fetched parent content.

anthropic-action-event-support.title: Claude Code Action event parsing at an immutable revision
anthropic-action-event-support.claim: This revision throws on discussion and discussion_comment before the agent can start. Other refs are not assumed to share that behavior.

anthropic-tag-pr-paths.title: Claude Code Action tag-mode PR prompt
anthropic-tag-pr-paths.claim: Tag mode builds a PR prompt that includes changed-file paths, which can originate in the PR head rather than from the triggering actor.

anthropic-app-token.title: Claude Code Action OIDC App token path
anthropic-app-token.claim: Without a supplied github_token, the Action can exchange an OIDC token for an App token with default contents, pull-requests, and issues write permissions.

anthropic-agent-prompt-787.title: Claude Code Action agent mode at the fixture's immutable revision
anthropic-agent-prompt-787.claim: Agent mode uses the configured prompt directly and forwards configured Claude tool arguments; it does not automatically append the Issue body.

anthropic-agent-token-787.title: Claude Code Action token setup at the fixture's immutable revision
anthropic-agent-token-787.claim: The Action exports its acquired GitHub token as GH_TOKEN before starting Claude; exact issued App-token scope and tool invocation remain unobserved.

anthropic-agent-oidc-787.title: Claude Code Action OIDC exchange at the fixture's immutable revision
anthropic-agent-oidc-787.claim: Without github_token, the Action attempts an OIDC-to-App token exchange; success and actual issued scope are external runtime facts.

anthropic-agent-mcp-787.title: Claude Code Action MCP setup at the fixture's immutable revision
anthropic-agent-mcp-787.claim: Agent mode does not install GitHub MCP tools unless they are explicitly allowed.

gh-issue-view.title: GitHub CLI issue view manual
gh-issue-view.claim: gh issue view displays an Issue's title, body, and other information.

checkout-protection.title: Safer pull_request_target defaults for GitHub Actions checkout
checkout-protection.claim: Current floating supported checkout majors refuse common fork-PR head and merge checkouts unless allow-unsafe-pr-checkout explicitly opts out; immutable and older refs require version-aware treatment.

permissions.title: GitHub Actions workflow syntax: permissions
permissions.claim: Workflow and job permissions determine the effective GITHUB_TOKEN capability.

reusable-workflows.title: Reuse workflows
reusable-workflows.claim: Local reusable workflows inherit caller context subject to explicit inputs, secrets, and permissions.

secrets-to-action.title: Secrets in GitHub Actions
secrets-to-action.claim: A secret must be set as an Action input or environment variable to make it available to that Action.

project-analysis-contract.title: AgentCI Guard analysis contract
project-analysis-contract.claim: Unknown permissions, unsupported event conditions, parse failures, and unresolved reusable workflows must be explicit diagnostics.

project-rule-contract.title: AgentCI Guard rule contract
project-rule-contract.claim: Agent identification, source, sink, capability, permission, pinning, and checkout behavior determine rule outcomes.

cases.rationale: A secret defined at workflow scope reaches an AI step unless a narrower scope replaces it.
A secret defined at job scope reaches each AI step unless the step replaces that key.
A secret explicitly mounted on an AI step is available to that step.
A non-secret job value replaces the same workflow-level secret key.
A non-secret step value replaces the same workflow-level secret key for that step.
An AI CLI invoked in run already executes through a shell and therefore has command capability.

targets: env launcher around a direct AI CLI
cases.rationale: GNU env runs Claude after a constant CI assignment; the comment body is a direct prompt argument in a writable AI job.
Prompt prose that mentions enabling shell or commands is not evidence that those tools were configured, and a full 40-hex Action ref is immutable for the pinning predicate.
Generic agent, User-Agent, Python, Node, shell, and non-agent inference credentials are not proof of an AI coding agent.
The job is reachable only on push, so pull_request_target-specific source and context are unreachable.
The job is reachable on pull_request_target and passes attacker-controlled PR content to the agent.
A job guarded by boolean false is unreachable on every configured event.
The OR and AND expression admits push but makes its pull_request_target branch impossible.
Negation removes pull_request_target from the reachable event set.
An unsupported event predicate must remain conservative and make the incomplete reachability analysis visible.
Omitted permissions depend on repository settings, so the scanner must abstain instead of assuming read or write.
An explicit read-all repository default closes the otherwise unknown permission boundary.
The untrusted prompt remains a source-to-sink finding, but job-level empty permissions remove token-write findings.
GitHub can trigger this workflow, but the verified Anthropic Action revision rejects discussion before Claude starts. No agent-mediated write path is claimed.
This synthetic Action ref has unverified discussion_comment support. The untrusted comment and write scope justify potential findings, not a confirmed agent-side effect.
This synthetic Action ref has unverified discussion_comment support. If it runs, comment content is untrusted; explicit discussions read must not create write-permission findings.
This synthetic Action ref has unverified discussion support. If it runs, title content is untrusted; explicit discussions read prevents token-write findings.
Malformed YAML cannot be analyzed and must produce an explicit error rather than a clean result.

Caller event, permission, untrusted input, and explicit capability context must propagate through a nested local reusable-workflow call chain. The literal prompt prefix guarantees agent mode while retaining transitive input taint. Contract change 2026-09-05, by owner decision after review of anthropics/claude-code-action docs/security.md: the callee is that action with its default write-access gate intact (no allowed_non_write_users or allowed_bots, no pull_request_target or discussion trigger, no untrusted text in a run: step), so the write-token finding is agentci/gated-ai-write-token at high rather than critical. See docs/analysis-model.md, 'The agent's own gate'.
A pinned agent with a trusted prompt and read-only permissions in a reachable local reusable workflow must be detected without producing a finding.

targets: inherited secret availability without Action exposure
cases.rationale: The caller makes secrets available to the reusable workflow, but the AI Action has no explicit secret input or environment reference. Inheritance alone is not an ai-with-secrets finding; the built-in workflow token is modeled separately.
A local call cycle prevents complete expansion and must be reported as partial analysis.
A missing local reusable workflow prevents complete expansion and must produce an explicit error instead of a clean result.
The scanner does not fetch remote workflow bodies, so the unresolved analysis boundary must be visible.
The step explicitly opts out of actions/checkout v7's unsafe-PR protection while requesting the pull request head.
The floating checkout v4 major receives GitHub's current unsafe-fork-PR protection and no opt-out is present, so the requested fork head is refused rather than checked out.
Checkout v1 is explicitly excluded from the protection backport and requests both the fork repository and pull request merge ref.
A fixed checkout SHA can refer to code before or after the protection and the selected action body is not resolved, so the scanner must abstain.
The default pull_request_target checkout uses the trusted base context rather than an explicit attacker-controlled head ref.
A third-party AI Action referenced by a mutable tag is not pinned to immutable content.
A workflow_call-only file with no reachable local caller lacks caller events, inputs, secrets, and permission context and must not look complete.
An action input explicitly enabling Bash is direct shell-capability evidence.

The bare action uses tag mode. A trusted commenter may trigger it on an attacker-authored parent Issue or PR; checking the commenter does not authenticate the fetched parent body. The write-token path remains critical despite the action's default trigger-user gate.

An external Issue creator can reach the explicit agent-mode prompt carrying their title. The pinned Action only honors allowed_non_write_users when github_token is supplied; this workflow supplies both, so its default trigger-user write-access gate no longer justifies a high-severity downgrade.

targets: trigger actor differs from parent Issue author
cases.rationale: The owner can apply a label to an attacker-authored Issue. The owner-only sender gate authenticates the labeler, not the author of the Issue body interpolated into the agent prompt. The actor-only job condition remains an event-reachability uncertainty.

targets: creation-only event connects sender to Issue body author
cases.rationale: On an issues.opened-only trigger, the gated sender created the Issue body. The owner-only gate removes untrusted-source findings, but the job still carries a broad write scope. The actor-only job condition remains an event-reachability uncertainty.

targets: trusted commenter differs from parent author
cases.rationale: A trusted owner comment can invoke tag mode on an attacker-authored parent Issue. Tag mode fetches the Issue body at runtime, so a commenter gate does not remove the parent-content write-token path. The actor-only job condition remains an event-reachability uncertainty.

targets: explicit agent-mode prompt does not self-fetch event content
cases.rationale: Providing a static prompt selects Anthropic agent mode, which writes that prompt directly. The scanner must not infer event-body ingestion merely because the trigger is issues.opened; the broad write scope remains independently reportable.

targets: Issue body read through an explicitly permitted agent tool
cases.rationale: The pinned Action receives a static prompt with the Issue number and a Bash allowlist for gh issue view. A write-authorized labeler may trigger it on an outsider-authored Issue. The tool could read that body, but the workflow alone cannot prove Claude invoked the tool or that the App token had a particular issued scope; the write-token path abstains rather than claiming a critical finding.

targets: Issue number without a permitted gh issue read tool
cases.rationale: The prompt passes only an Issue number, not the body. This pinned Action's agent mode does not automatically fetch the body, and its configured Bash allowlist lacks gh issue view. No supported Issue-body ingestion path is established by this fixture; the unrelated shell, secret, and write-permission observations remain.

targets: PR head provenance differs from review-comment author
cases.rationale: A same-repository PR head says nothing about who wrote a review comment. The comment body reaches the prompt; the action's default commenter write-access check only changes the write-token severity to high. The provenance-only job condition remains an event-reachability uncertainty.

targets: owner actor does not authenticate fork PR changed-file paths
cases.rationale: A repository owner may open a PR from another person's fork. track_progress forces tag mode even with a static prompt, and that mode includes PR changed-file paths from the head branch. The owner gate does not authenticate those paths; id-token: write with no supplied github_token models a potential separate App write capability, not a writable fork-PR GITHUB_TOKEN. The actor-only condition leaves event reachability partially unresolved.

targets: fork PR changed-file paths in tag mode
cases.rationale: A fork PR author controls changed-file paths that tag mode includes in the agent context. The Action's actor gate cannot downgrade this source-aware finding; the modeled write path is a potential OIDC App token, not the workflow's read-only GITHUB_TOKEN.

Review finding 3 (2026-09-05): the Gemini CLI action was absent from the detector, so untrusted comment text reaching Gemini in a write-token job scanned as no agent, no findings, complete. The action operates on the triggering event's issue or PR (its github_issue_number and github_pr_number inputs default to the payload) and documents no write-access gate, so it is treated like the other agent actions.

targets: agent detection precision: same vendor organization, non-agent actions
cases.rationale: google-github-actions publishes auth, setup-gcloud, and deploy actions that are not agents. Matching the organization instead of the exact repository would flag ordinary deployment workflows; this case pins that they stay silent even on an untrusted event with a write token.

targets: agent detection precision: owner identity is exact
cases.rationale: Follow-up review (2026-09-09): an owner such as not-google-github-actions matched the Gemini pattern because a hyphen is a word boundary, and this exact fixture produced a critical finding. A uses: reference names its owner first; the matcher now requires the vendor match at the start of the reference, for every vendor. The same shape with the real owner is the gemini-write case.
